stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context in robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical achievement.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement for robots.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning introduces harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack methodology extends beyond previous, limited studies that focused on small, established data sources like Wikipedia.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a new framework for robot policies that significantly scales visuomotor context up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a major technical hurdle overcome.
Enables advanced capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

The context is centered around text generation using transformer-based models.

The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is currently serving a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing the MLX framework.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates MLX, Apple's native machine learning framework.
This integration aims to provide the fastest possible performance for running Ollama on Apple Silicon.
The feature is currently available in a preview state.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool aims to bring powerful AI capabilities directly to the user's personal device.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is launching satellites specifically for wildfire detection.
The new system is designed to identify wildfires that existing satellite technology often misses.
The deployment is timely, addressing severe wildfire smoke impacting the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The action targets apps designed to influence user behavior, suggesting regulatory scrutiny over manipulative design patterns.
The ordinance implies that Google and Apple likely generated significant revenue from these types of applications.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: Introduces SceneBind, an omni-modal representation designed to fuse vision, audio, and language data.
Addresses a key limitation in existing models by explicitly integrating 3D spatial understanding alongside semantic information.
Represents scenes as semantic-spatial entities using a combination of global and object-centric embeddings.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the scalability and manual difficulty of quantitative evidence synthesis across various fields (science, medicine, policy).
The system automates the entire process, from formulating search strategies based on natural language questions to extracting data from full-text studies.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap between text-level safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that linguistically harmless instructions can lead to dangerous physical outcomes when grounded in the real world.
Uses hidden-state direction analysis to show that 'content danger' and 'physical danger' are separable signals within LLM representations.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
Previous poisoning research was limited to small, established datasets (like Wikipedia) and ignored real-world corpus heterogeneity.
The study highlights the difficulty in detecting and mitigating harmful behaviors introduced by poisoned pretraining data.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models across various hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It integrates built-in support for Ollama, a popular local LLM runner.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: A government pilot program is testing the use of AI in insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the dual potential of AI: solving bureaucratic hurdles like prior authorization or exacerbating them.
This touches upon the intersection of healthcare administration, regulatory technology (RegTech), and AI ethics.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagramEdit, a system designed to automate the editing of scientific diagrams in research papers.
The system aims to allow authors to modify figures (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
The challenge addressed is the complexity of scientific figures, which are dense infographics composed of heterogeneous visual elements.

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper introduces a new evaluation paradigm for AI security agents that incorporates operational cost alongside success rate.
Current security evaluations often overlook the resource consumption (inference budget) of reasoning steps and tool calls in real-world scenarios.
The research tests these cost-aware metrics on both offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security tasks.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve open-domain information-seeking.
Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM agents: getting stuck in repetitive search loops when initial queries fail.
Focuses on enhancing task progress tracking and search efficiency in complex, multi-step information retrieval tasks.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., 'How does rain affect traffic?') using purely observational data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations to enable deeper insights.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training corpus priorities, leading to inefficiencies when new languages are added.
Adding new languages to fixed tokenizers can increase token count per word, negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy usage.
The paper proposes an 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' method to address these limitations, particularly for compact models where embedding matrices are constrained.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of traditional Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes an 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' to overcome the trade-off between long-horizon memory and real-time performance.

stories.title: Decoding Market Emotion from Blockchain Activity: A Data-Driven Sentiment Classifier
stories.author: Bruno L. Dalmazo
bullet_points: The research proposes a novel sentiment classification model for Bitcoin market analysis.
The model integrates three data sources: on-chain blockchain activity, historical price data, and Twitter sentiment.
The primary focus is on explaining market sentiment rather than predicting future price movements.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences efficiently.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates as new user ratings arrive, improving real-time relevance.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The issue is more critical for compact models where embedding matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of shared neurons.
Proposes a mechanism for continuous-valued signal routing where hidden neurons are physically shared across multiple computational paths.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a promising area for embodied control, linking action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robustness and safety.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the failure modes of these advanced control models.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagramEdit, a system designed to automate the editing of scientific diagrams in research papers.
The system aims to allow authors to modify complex figures (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the dense, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific infographics, which the model must understand.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval system evaluation (static usefulness) fails when language models act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a document in agentic search depends on its potential to enable future actions, not just its relevance to the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses GI endoscopy case studies to compare nine existing systems, highlighting the gap between high benchmark performance and faithful clinical reasoning.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves challenge performance, the paper suggests that performance gains do not guarantee complete or accurate clinical explanations.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis in TikTok political conversations.
Addresses the current gap in computational analysis by combining audiovisual information with conversational context from short-video platforms.
The dataset is built from 161 TikTok videos and 13,876 comments, focusing on the 2024 U.S. election cycle.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The issue is particularly critical for compact models, as large vocabularies strain embedding and LM-head matrices.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of multilingual PLMs on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages due to tokenizer limitations.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed for Amharic and Tigrinya (Ge'ez-script languages).
Evaluates the proposed model across 19 total African languages, including 17 additional low-resource varieties.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Identifies a limitation in existing methods: they approximate log-likelihood by ignoring the sequential nature of unmasking during generation.
Proposes a novel approach, 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients,' to account for the two decisions made at each generation step.

stories.title: GPT-5.6 used a prompt to close a 30-year gap in convex optimization
stories.author: mbustamanter
bullet_points: GPT-5.6 demonstrated an ability to solve a long-standing problem in convex optimization.
The achievement reportedly closed a 30-year gap in the field of convex optimization.
The success was achieved by utilizing a specific prompt, highlighting the power of LLMs in complex mathematical tasks.

stories.title: NextBSD project revived: Apple's FOSS user-space tools on the FreeBSD kernel
stories.author: nextbsd.org via lproven
bullet_points: The NextBSD project has been revived, focusing on integrating Apple's FOSS user-space tools.
This effort aims to bring Apple's open-source components into the FreeBSD kernel environment.
The news is relevant to the open-source community and operating system development.

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge: porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2.
The porting process encountered significant difficulties, including a dual-path FFN and a non-traceable sparse expert loop.
A critical bug was identified where the device output was empty despite perfect CPU reference results and passing unit tests, highlighting deployment complexities.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex deployment challenge: porting a large language model (Gemma-4 31B) to AWS Inferentia2.
A standard tensor-parallel recipe that succeeded at a smaller model size (12B) failed when scaled to 31B.
The author notes a critical issue where validation passes despite the model producing incorrect ('garbage') outputs, highlighting potential pitfalls in deployment pipelines.
